headline: Medium risk: shared networked data flows and MCP-enabled Haystack can amplify leakage and cascading errors; no direct prompt-injection bridge is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airbyte exposes API-based data flows and broad network egress, while Haystack can use MCP servers. That creates a plausible bridge only if an operator wires Airbyte outputs into Haystack inputs or an MCP tool path; no direct shared channel is documented, so the interaction is possible but not default-dangerous.
conditions: IF Airbyte output is copied into a Haystack prompt or MCP tool input without sanitization, injection becomes plausible.
IF both agents are connected through a shared filesystem, queue, or MCP server, attacker-controlled content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Disable any automatic handoff from Airbyte exports into Haystack prompts.
Add a manual review step before Haystack consumes Airbyte-generated text.
Restrict MCP servers to trusted, allowlisted tools.
Use separate workspaces for each agent.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on all inter-agent payloads.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress; Haystack also has broad network egress and can call MCP servers. Even without a documented shared workspace, a paired deployment can leak business data if Airbyte-fed content is routed into Haystack or if Haystack forwards context to external services.
conditions: IF Airbyte ingests business data that is later passed to Haystack, sensitive content can leave the original boundary.
IF Haystack is configured to call external APIs or MCP tools on Airbyte-derived content, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Keep Airbyte and Haystack on separate networks.
Block outbound traffic from Haystack except to approved endpoints.
Redact business data before any Haystack ingestion.
Review MCP tool allowlists before enabling them.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention controls on inter-agent transfers.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, but the profiles do not show overlapping filesystem write, git, or shared mutable-resource scopes. The main conflict surface is limited to network/API contention, which is narrower than the rubric’s medium/high write-conflict cases.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external API quota or rate-limited endpoint, they can contend for capacity.
IF an operator grants both write access to the same downstream system, conflicts become more serious.
mitigations: Separate API credentials per agent.
Set per-agent rate limits.
Avoid sharing mutable destinations.
Monitor for 429s and retry storms.
requires-engineering: add locking for shared downstream writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a search-RAG system and can consume outputs from other systems, while Airbyte produces data pipelines and API-fed outputs. If Haystack treats Airbyte output as authoritative, errors or malformed records can cascade into downstream answers or actions; no verification step is documented in either profile.
conditions: IF Haystack ingests Airbyte-produced records without validation, upstream errors can propagate into generated answers.
IF downstream automation trusts Haystack outputs, a bad Airbyte record can cascade into incorrect actions.
mitigations: Add schema validation before Haystack ingestion.
Require source citations in Haystack outputs.
Quarantine new Airbyte feeds until sampled.
Log and review mismatches between source and retrieved text.
requires-engineering: implement confidence thresholds before downstream action.

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and Haystack touches anonymous usage statistics, so the profiles do not show a direct residency or regulated-data mismatch. The main compliance concern is policy drift if business data is routed into Haystack’s telemetry or external APIs; that is plausible but not documented here.
conditions: IF business data is routed into Haystack telemetry or external API calls, retention and residency policies may diverge.
IF the deployment handles regulated data classes not listed in either profile, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Keep business data out of telemetry fields.
Review retention settings for both systems.
Disable unnecessary analytics exports.
Document data-class boundaries for operators.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data-class routing.
